--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_geographical_threshold_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add a geographical threshold graph, in which heavy or nearby nodes are joined. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_geographical_threshold_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add a geographical threshold graph, in which heavy or nearby nodes are joined. title: >- [Graph.add_geographical_threshold_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a geographical threshold graph, in which heavy or nearby nodes are joined. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a geographical threshold graph, in which heavy or nearby nodes are joined. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15785-L15979){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_geographical_threshold_graph( n, theta, dim=2, p_norm=2.0, p_dist=None, seed=None, pos_attr="pos", node_weight_attr="weight", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Geographical threshold graph](../assets/graphs/add-geographical-threshold-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three geographical threshold graphs on the same seven random points, each node shaded by its random weight, darker for heavier, at threshold theta=80, 30, and 10. Two nodes are joined when their combined weight divided by their squared distance reaches theta, so heavy nodes reach far: at theta=80 only the heaviest node has edges, 2 of them, and at theta=10 it has 6 of the 13." width="100%"} Gives each of `n` nodes a random weight, drawn from an exponential distribution with mean `1`, and a position drawn uniformly from the unit cube `[0, 1]^dim`. Two nodes `u` and `v` at distance `d` are joined when `(w_u + w_v) * p_dist(d) >= theta`; by default `p_dist(d) = d ** -2`, so the rule is `(w_u + w_v) / d ** 2 >= theta`. Heavy nodes therefore link over long distances and light ones only to close neighbors, which yields hubs in a spatial graph. Once the weights and positions are drawn there is no further randomness, and a larger `theta` gives a sparser graph. Distance is the Minkowski distance of order `p_norm`. The model is due to Masuda, Miwa and Konno; the process follows NetworkX's `geographical_threshold_graph()`. Each node's position is stored as a list of `dim` coordinates in the `pos_attr=` node attribute, and its weight in the `node_weight_attr=` node attribute. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Geographical threshold graphs are useful for: - spatial networks with hubs, such as airline routes or trade between cities - modeling links that need enough combined mass to bridge a distance - studying how a single threshold controls density and degree heterogeneity ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [theta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Threshold that `(w_u + w_v) * p_dist(d)` must reach for a link. [dim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of dimensions of the unit cube. Default is `2`. Must be at least `1`. [p_norm]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Order of the Minkowski distance: `1.0` for Manhattan, `2.0` (default) for Euclidean, or `float("inf")` for Chebyshev. Must be positive. [p_dist]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[float], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Function of the distance `d` that scales the combined weight. It is called once for each pair of nodes. If `None` (default), `d ** -2` is used. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [pos_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pos"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's position. Default is `"pos"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [node_weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["weight"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's weight. Default is `"weight"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative, `theta=` is NaN, `dim=` is less than `1`, or `p_norm=` is not positive. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_random_geometric_graph`) : Join points by distance alone. [](`~add_soft_random_geometric_graph`) : Join points within a radius with a distance-based chance. [](`~add_waxman_graph`) : Join any two points with a chance that decays with distance. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A hundred nodes with threshold `100`: ::: {#99207c47 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_geographical_threshold_graph( n=100, theta=100, seed=10 ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 311) ``` ::: ::: Heavier nodes reach farther, so the heaviest node has more neighbors than the lightest: ::: {#ffc669f8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} weights = graph.get_node_attrs("weight") heaviest = max(weights, key=weights.get) lightest = min(weights, key=weights.get) graph.get_degree(heaviest), graph.get_degree(lightest) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (12, 6) ``` ::: ::: Raising `theta=` thins the graph out: ::: {#8ecaf35e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ ec.Graph() .add_geographical_threshold_graph(n=100, theta=theta, seed=10) .count_edges() for theta in (25, 50, 100, 200) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [1090, 585, 311, 164] ``` ::: ::: ### A low threshold or a high one Forty nodes at the same positions and with the same weights, drawn where they sit and colored by weight, with `theta=30` on the left and `theta=120` on the right. Raising the threshold cuts the edges to about a third, and the light nodes lose theirs first, so that several are left with none. The heaviest node keeps `5` of its `19` neighbors: ::: {#4eda75a5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} def threshold(theta): return ec.Graph().add_geographical_threshold_graph( n=40, theta=theta, seed=1 ) low, high = threshold(30), threshold(120) weights = low.get_node_attrs("weight") heaviest = max(weights, key=weights.get) [(g.count_edges(), g.get_degree(heaviest)) for g in (low, high)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [(131, 19), (45, 5)] ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#c98459e1 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} low.plot( layout="pos", color_by="weight", show_labels=False, node_size=7, width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
